title: GitLab patches a critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed servers, affecting every release since 7.0 in 2014 (Swati Khandelwal/The Hacker News)
title_en: GitLab patches a critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers run code on self-managed servers, affecting every release since 7.0 in 2014 (Swati Khandelwal/The Hacker News)
author: The Hacker News
content_snippet:
GitLab released fixes on October 21 for a flaw that lets an attacker run code on a self-managed server without logging in, and it affects every version of the software going back to 7.0, released in 2014.

The fix matters even for administrators who patched nine days earlier: the October 12 update covered only versions 19.2 and later, and the new fixed versions sit one patch above it, so an instance updated then is in range again.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, is rated 10.0 on the CVSS
summary_en: GitLab released an urgent patch for CVE-2026-110264, a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated remote code execution on self-managed servers. The vulnerability affects all versions since 2014 and is rated at the maximum 10.0 CVSS score.

summary_en: Nvidia unveiled the DSX POD modular data center reference design at GTC Berlin, built around Vera Rubin systems. author: Wired AI
content_snippet:

Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.

summary_en: Security researchers from Claroc discovered a design flaw in Meta's AI app Muse, allowing attackers to easily enumerate shared conversation links. Despite Zuckerberg's claims of privacy-first architecture, the predictable URL structure allowed researchers to harvest thousands of sensitive private chats with a single query.

author: MIT Tech Review

summary_en: Researchers are deciphering the molecular cascade triggered by physical activity to develop pills that mimic the health perks of exercise for frail and chronically ill individuals. title: Claude Science tackles deadly scorpion stings by designing protein binders from scratch
